When I was little, I got a chemistry set, but it was pretty well and good castrated even then. While the chemistry sets in the '50s and '60s could potentially let you build a nuclear reactors or blown off your hands, none of the chemicals in mine did anything worse than stain the rug. He's only seven right now, but his inner masculine pyro side is already showing itself (as evidenced by his begging to ignite thermite the last time I saw him), and I want to help make sure the kid doesn't wind up a sad, broken shell of a man with no prospects when he grows up, while also trying not to be the deciding factor in his becoming a convicted felon.

I figure exposure to science and sparking the questions of 'how', 'why', and 'what if' are the best things I can offer him. I'd strongly recommend Arduino if he has any interest in electronics whatsoever. The number of things you can do with a $50 Arduino starter kit is absolutely unreal. The ATtiny85 chips are also incredibly useful, for those little projects that you want logical handling but don't want to drop an entire $20 board for.

Also, chemistry sets are lame these days but most of the precursor chemicals are still very very approachable in cost. If you really do want to go that route with him, just pick a project and investigate that one specifically instead of trying to get a catch-all set of equipment. It's a great way to follow the scientific method with him as well.

For example: what happens if you compress the thermite vs. leave it as a powder? How does it handle a binder like playdoh or paraffin? If you crack up a few sparklers into bits and mix them in, what does that do to the ignition rate? Can it burn underwater?

He's a little young yet, but in a couple years you should look at sparkfun.com and pickup some of the beginner kits.

As someone else mentioned, getting a model rocket could be fun as well and if his parents don't like the idea of a real rocket you could look into water rockets (easier and can be a lot of fun for kids that age). You can build a water rocket from scratch (2L pop bottle) or buy ready built kits.
